title: Minimal-impact status brief — transient model-routing loop and recovery options
body:
Purpose
This note is a concise customer-facing status update and short post-incident summary for a transient model-routing loop that affected a subset of streaming requests on 2026-07-21. It is intended for product and enterprise customers who want a brief explanation, verification steps, and options for recovery or mitigation.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- What happened: For ~25 minutes between 09:12–09:37 UTC on 2026-07-21, an internal routing edge-case caused a small percentage of streaming generation requests to be routed in a loop between routing layers, introducing extra hops and delaying chunk acknowledgments. A further small subset of those sessions observed partial or out-of-order chunks before automatic recovery kicked in.
- Customer impact: ~0.4% of streaming sessions across multiple regions experienced elevated latency (median additional 350–700 ms per chunk) and ~0.05% showed partial chunk duplication or ordering anomalies. Non-streaming text generation and embeddings were not affected. No customer data was lost.
- Current status: Service fully recovered at 09:37 UTC; additional safeguards are in place. We are sharing verification steps and optional customer actions below.

What went wrong (brief)
- A routing policy change (deployed as part of a capacity optimization) introduced a path selection mismatch when routes were rapidly rebalanced under brief scale events. In specific timing windows the control plane retried route selection and returned a secondary route while the primary route was still handling a session, producing duplicate in-flight route entries. That state caused a small number of streaming requests to traverse an extra hop and, in rare cases, observe duplicate chunk delivery or reordering.

Timeline (high level)
- 09:11 UTC: Capacity rebalance event triggered by autoscaler scale-out.
- 09:12 UTC: First customer reports of delayed streaming chunks; internal alerts fired for elevated chunk latency and duplicate chunk metrics.
- 09:15 UTC: SRE and runtime teams identify a routing selection race condition and deploy a short-term rule to prefer pinned routes for ongoing sessions (mitigant 1).
- 09:22 UTC: Metric anomalies persist for smaller percentage; mitigation 2 (control-plane retry backoff adjustment) deployed.
- 09:37 UTC: Streaming metrics return to baseline; no new customer reports. Post-deploy monitoring shows stable routing decisions.

Impact details for customers
- Affected customers: Tenants with high-concurrency streaming workloads during the 09:12–09:37 UTC window. We estimate roughly 0.4% of streaming sessions experienced latency increase; 0.05% observed partial duplication or ordering anomalies.
- Scope: Limited to streaming API sessions (server-sent events / chunked responses). Synchronous non-stream endpoints (single response) and embeddings pipelines were unaffected.
- Data integrity: No tokens were dropped. Where duplication occurred, tokens were repeated; we provide guidance for deduplication verification below.

What we did (mitigations and fixes applied)
Short-term actions (incident window)
- Immediately enforced pinned-route preference for in-flight sessions to avoid switching mid-session.
- Tuned control-plane retry/backoff behavior to prevent rapid alternate-route selection.
- Temporarily increased streaming observability retention for detailed replay and verification.

Stabilization (within 2 hours)
- Rolled a small config update to add a lightweight session stamp that prevents multiple concurrent route bindings for the same session id.
- Added alert thresholds for chunk duplication and out-of-order delivery to escalate earlier.

Planned follow-up (permanent fix)
- Replace the short-term session stamp with a robust route-lease mechanism (engineering RFC approved, scheduled sprint 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-12).
- Add deterministic replay tooling so customers and support teams can request a session replay bundle within 30 days for impacted sessions.
- Expand simulation coverage in the routing test harness to include aggressive autoscaler scale events.

Customer verification steps (what you can do)
- If you saw delayed chunks: check your client-side stream ACK timings against server timestamps (response "chunk_received_at" header) — increased per-chunk latency will be visible as a consistent delta in that time window.
- If you suspect duplicated tokens or ordering issues: fetch the session logs (if you log full chunks client-side) and compare to the server-side replay package we can provide. Duplicate tokens will be contiguous or match repeated chunk payloads.
- If you use exactly-once semantics in your application: consider adding an idempotency key at the chunk or message level (we provide pattern suggestions below).

Optional customer recovery choices we can help with
- Request a verified replay and evidence package: our operations team can produce a bundle of server and routing traces for every reported session — useful for debugging app-level dedup logic or for audit.
- Apply proactive client-side deduplication: we can share a short library snippet (Node/Python/Go) that deduplicates contiguous chunk duplicates and reorders by server-provided chunk sequence numbers.
- Elect a targeted tenant rollback window: for enterprise tenants that require it, we can offer to reprocess affected requests with a higher-priority route for a limited grace period. This is manual and requires coordination.

Short sample messages for customers (editable)
- Status page blurb (90 chars): "Brief routing anomaly caused short-lived streaming delays for a small set of sessions. Service recovered; next steps posted."
- Extended update (for console/email): "Between 09:12–09:37 UTC we observed a routing selection loop affecting a small percentage of streaming sessions. We applied mitigations, restored normal routing, and are providing verification bundles on request. No data loss occurred; guidance and remediation options are available."

Evidence and transparency
- We will publish a longer postmortem on our status site within 72 hours with a deeper technical root cause analysis and a timeline of code changes.
- If you need direct evidence for audits, contact your account lead and we will provide a replay/evidence package (signed and hashed) for affected sessions.

How to contact us
- Open a support ticket via the Console (Support > Incidents) and reference "routing-loop-2026-07-21" for priority handling.
- For enterprise accounts, contact your SAG/CSM and we will escalate to Eng+SRE with a target response in 4 business hours.

Notes to internal readers
- Suggested internal next steps: coordinate with runtime owners on the route-lease RFC prioritization and ensure the replay bundle work is staffed for Sprint 34. Update the status site with the full postmortem by 2026-07-24.

Appendix: quick dedupe pattern (example)
- Include a chunk-level sequence header: X-Chunk-Seq: <n>
- On client receive: if seq == last_seq => drop duplicate; if seq > last_seq+1 => flag missing chunk and optionally request server-side replay.

End of brief

Draft approvals: please review for technical accuracy (eng-routing), compliance language (security/compliance), and customer tone (customer-success).
